Brazil's national delegation welcomes strengthened cooperation between the Office of the Prosecutor and Libyan authorities and a more positive trajectory. Complementarity is central: national jurisdictions have the primary duty; the ICC acts only when a State is unable or unwilling. Nonparties have no Rome Statute obligations, yet Resolution 1970 (2011) under Chapter VII requires Libyan authorities to cooperate fully. Other States and organizations are urged to cooperate; the ICC has no enforcement instruments and depends on States, so its cooperation requests must conform to the Statute and relevant Council resolutions.

We welcome the improved cooperation trajectory. No ICC judgments exist in the Libyan situation so far, but evidence collection and investigative progress are welcome. Transparency matters: we ask for additional information on the four key lines of inquiry. We hope fruitful OTP-Libyan relations, grounded in complementarity, will deliver justice and accountability.

Victim empowerment matters inside and outside Libya; further engagement with victims and their representatives is encouraged. Justice must avoid politicization, selectivity and double standards; all victims of the most serious crimes must be treated equally regardless of the situation under investigation.<|im_end|>
